engagement_summary.substance_name: Bovine lactoferrin produced by a modified strain of Komagataella phaffii (ALLGLF)
engagement_summary.notifier: All G Co Holdings Pty Limited (agent: Vireo Advisors, LLC)
engagement_summary.production_method: Precision fermentation using genetically modified K. phaffii strain Ppas_337
engagement_summary.source_organism: Komagataella phaffii Ppas_337 expressing Bos taurus lactoferrin variant A gene
intended_uses: Dairy and plant-based yogurt products (100 mg/100g)
engagement_summary.target_population: General population including infants and young children; not intended for infant formula
engagement_summary.submission_completeness_note: All Parts 1-7 present with four appendices. Two rounds of FDA questions (Jan and Feb-Mar 2026) were answered with amendments adding Cronobacter and cereulide specifications, correcting EDI table errors, and removing non-substitutional claim.

categorical_eligibility.basis: Fermentation-derived food protein assessed via scientific procedures under 21 CFR 170.30(a) and (b); K. phaffii platform has multiple prior GRAS no-questions letters

scope_clarity.notes: Probiotic drinks removed via amendment. Use levels expressed per 100g or per serving with RACC basis documented. Technical function: alternative lactoferrin source.

existing_regulatory_status.prior_gras_notices: GRN 77, 130, 464, 465, 669 (milk-derived bLF no-questions); GRN 1219 (recombinant bLF from K. phaffii, no-questions confirmed during review)
existing_regulatory_status.food_additive_approvals: 21 CFR 573.587 (K. phaffii in animal feed; confirmed not relied upon for human food safety conclusion)
existing_regulatory_status.notes: GRN 1219 (TurtleTree recombinant bLF from K. phaffii) received no-questions letter; closely analogous precedent cited in amendment.

potential_safety_signals.signal: High-mannose and phosphomannose glycans differ from native bLF
potential_safety_signals.evidence: ALLGLF lacks hybrid/complex glycans present in bovine bLF; contains phosphomannose (23.73%) and Man10-13 absent in native bLF. Literature citation (Feng et al., 2025) raised theoretical immunogenicity concern for yeast high-mannose glycans.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Amendment response addresses this adequately by referencing GRN 1219 CD-SIGN/TLR4 data and oral tolerance mechanisms; no additional data appear required based on reviewed content.

potential_safety_signals.signal: Infant and young child exposure to fermentation-derived protein without culture collection deposit
potential_safety_signals.evidence: NHANES data show ~31% infant consumption. Production strain Ppas_337 not deposited in recognized culture collection; confirmed in March 2026 amendment.
potential_safety_signals.recommended_action: Submission acknowledges lack of deposit; internal characterization via WGS, PCR, and Sanger sequencing provided as substitute. In this assessment, this represents a residual documentation issue rather than a safety gap given the extensive genetic characterization provided.

identity_and_characterization.summary: ALLGLF identity is well-characterized via seven orthogonal physicochemical methods demonstrating high similarity to native bLF. Glycan differences (phosphomannose, Man10-13, absence of hybrid/complex types) are documented and contextualized. Peer-reviewed publication (Cavallo et al., 2025) covers characterization data.

strengths.observation: 100% amino acid sequence coverage confirmed by LC-MS/MS with 867 unique peptides; full bLF sequence verified
Seven-method physicochemical comparability package (SDS-PAGE, LC-MS/MS, glycan profiling, iron binding, IEP, CD, DSC) with food-grade commercial bLF as comparator
Glycan differences acknowledged and functionally assessed; no impact on structure, thermostability, charge, or iron binding documented

gaps.title: No in vitro pepsin digestibility data for ALLGLF itself
gaps.observation: Digestibility addressed in amendment via literature on native bLF (Troost et al., 2001; Dupont et al., 2020) but no pepsin digestibility data specifically for ALLGLF with its distinct glycan profile were presented. Glycan differences could theoretically affect digestion rate.

manufacturing_process.summary: Manufacturing process is described at a high level with seven steps from cell bank through spray drying. Strain construction is well-documented including auxotrophic selection, absence of antibiotic resistance, and WGS confirmation. Processing aids confirmed GRAS/FCC/USP via amendment.

strengths.observation: Deep WGS at 245X coverage confirmed only intended modifications; no antibiotic resistance genes or E. coli sequences detected
Genetic stability confirmed by PCR and Sanger sequencing over 87 generations, exceeding typical ~35 fermentation generations
Absence of production organism DNA in final product confirmed by PCR in three non-consecutive batches (LOD 10 fg/µL)

gaps.title: Chromatography resin identity and validation not specified
gaps.observation: Process description states 'chromatography step' for lactoferrin purification without specifying resin type, ligand, or potential leachables. Amendment confirms materials are GRAS/FCC/USP but chromatography resin leachables are not explicitly addressed.

gaps.title: Fermentation media composition not disclosed
gaps.observation: Fermentation media components (Syn6 medium referenced in Appendix II but not in main process description) and carbon sources are not enumerated in Part 2. Amendment confirms GRAS compliance but no list of specific media components is provided.

dietary_exposure.summary: EDI used NHANES 2021-2023 WWEIA data on a consumers-only basis with NHANES sample weights. Amendments corrected a %users calculation error and added 2+ year population strata. Cumulative exposure including GRN 464 background sources calculated. Substitutionality claim for GRN 77/464 withdrawn per FDA request.

strengths.observation: NHANES 2021-2023 most recent cycle used; food codes provided in Appendix IV; maximum use levels applied conservatively assuming full market penetration
Subpopulation breakdowns by age/sex including infants, toddlers, children, teenagers, and adults; body-weight-normalized estimates provided
Cumulative exposure including GRN 464 background sources and breast milk/formula context for infant exposures quantified and compared to prior safe-use levels

gaps.title: Consumers-only basis not converted to total-population (all-sample) estimate
gaps.observation: EDI is reported exclusively on consumers-only basis. Standard FDA practice requests total-sample (all-person) mean before presenting eaters-only. Amendment added 2+ stratum but retained consumers-only framing throughout; all-sample estimates were not generated.

safety_data.summary: Robust toxicological dataset for native bLF including acute, 4-week, 13-week subchronic, and 40-65 week chronic rat studies; NOAEL >2000 mg/kg/day established in multiple independent studies. Human clinical data from multiple RCTs up to 9 g/day. Rhesus monkey and recombinant human lactoferrin supportive data also cited. MOE >100 for all age groups >1 year.

strengths.observation: NOAEL >2000 mg/kg/day confirmed by 4-week and 13-week subchronic rat studies (Nishimura 1991/1997; Yamauchi et al., 2000) and 60-65 week chronic feeding study (Tamano et al., 2008)
Human RCT (Peterson et al., 2024) with rhLF produced in K. phaffii at up to 3.4 g/day for 28 days; no adverse effects; immunogenicity without clinical allergy
Post-submission literature search (64 records through Jan 2026) identified no contradicting safety information; Feng et al. 2025 glycan immunogenicity concern addressed with mechanistic rationale

gaps.title: No genotoxicity data presented
gaps.observation: No Ames test, chromosomal aberration, or in vitro micronucleus data are cited. Submission relies entirely on NOAEL from repeat-dose studies and EFSA/FDA prior evaluations. It is not clear whether genotoxicity studies exist for bLF or whether prior GRAS notices addressed this.

gaps.title: Reproductive/developmental toxicity data not addressed
gaps.observation: No reproductive or developmental toxicity studies cited. Given infant/toddler exposure and use by pregnant/lactating women consuming yogurt and beverages, the absence of this dataset is notable, though prior FDA no-questions letters may have accepted this gap for native bLF.

gaps.title: Safety studies conducted on native bLF or rhLF, not ALLGLF itself
gaps.observation: All pivotal toxicological studies used native bLF or recombinant human lactoferrin. ALLGLF has distinct glycan profile (phosphomannose, Man10-13). Bridging argument relies on physicochemical similarity; no ALLGLF-specific subacute or subchronic data were generated.

general_availability.summary: Core characterization data published in peer-reviewed open-access journal (Cavallo et al., 2025, Food Hydrocolloids). Pivotal toxicological studies for bLF are published (Yamauchi et al., 2000; Tamano et al., 2008) or publicly available through prior GRAS notices. EFSA 2012 opinion publicly available.

strengths.observation: Characterization data peer-reviewed and published open-access (Cavallo et al., 2025); glycan profiling conducted by accredited external facility (APAF, Macquarie University)
All key references are published in peer-reviewed journals; no pivotal data appear to be exclusively trade secret or unpublished

gaps.title: Internal LC-MS/MS purity method not published or independently validated
gaps.observation: Allergenicity/purity LC-MS/MS analysis conducted using in-house method. Methodology described in Appendix I but not published or third-party validated. Amendment confirms specifications methods validated but allergenicity LC-MS/MS is an in-house assay.

general_acceptance.summary: Strong authoritative body support from EFSA (2012 safety opinion, QPS status for K. phaffii) and multiple FDA no-questions letters for native and recombinant bLF (GRN 77, 130, 464, 465, 669, 1219). No identified scientific controversy specific to bLF safety at proposed use levels. GRN 1219 (analogous substance, same host organism) received no-questions letter during review period.

strengths.observation: EFSA 2012 concluded bLF safe for foods including infant formula; EU authorization covers broader uses than proposed
GRN 1219 (TurtleTree recombinant bLF from K. phaffii) received no-questions letter; directly analogous precedent cited in amendment response

gaps.title: No independent expert panel convened
gaps.observation: GRAS conclusion appears to have been made by the notifier's team without a convened independent expert panel review. This is permissible under self-affirmed GRAS but reduces transparency of the general acceptance determination.

conditions_of_use.summary: Eight food categories with maximum use levels specified. RACC basis for per-serving units documented per 21 CFR 101.12. Infant formula excluded. Probiotic drinks removed via amendment. Technical function (alternative lactoferrin source) and intended population (general, all ages) stated.

strengths.observation: All use levels expressed with consistent units; per-serving levels converted to mg/100g equivalents using RACC for exposure calculations
Explicit exclusion of infant formula and USDA-regulated products; labeling commitment for milk protein declaration under FALCPA

gaps.title: No minimum use level or typical use level specified
gaps.observation: Only maximum use levels provided. Typical or anticipated use levels would support more refined exposure estimates. This is a presentation gap and does not affect the conservative safety margin.

regulatory_submission.summary: All seven Parts present with four appendices. Dual certification provided (cover letter by agent; FDA Form 3667 signed by agent). FDA engaged with two rounds of written questions (Jan and Feb-Mar 2026), all substantively answered. Calculation error in Table 7 corrected in amendment.

strengths.observation: Balanced certification per 21 CFR 170.225; unfavorable Feng et al. 2025 immunogenicity concern identified and addressed in literature search amendment
FDA Form 3667 complete; presubmission meeting held March 2025; no trade secret designations; FOIA disclosure authorized for Parts 2-7

gaps.title: Certification signed by agent rather than notifier
gaps.observation: Both the cover letter certification and FDA Form 3667 are signed by Vireo Advisors (agent), not All G Co Holdings (notifier). Authorization letter reportedly included but agent-signed certification may warrant verification that it meets 21 CFR 170.225(c) requirements.
